title: Enterprise optimization intake: signal classifier and routing workflow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Replace the current ad-hoc intake spreadsheet and manual triage with an automated signal classifier that tags incoming optimization/advisory requests (batching, caching, quantization, routing) and routes them into appropriate lanes (self-serve suggestions, concierge advisory, enterprise SLA queue, or engineering backlog). The classifier will use request metadata + usage telemetry to assign a risk/ROI score and primary recommendation type.
background: We receive ~120 optimization requests/month across hosted and dedicated customers. Enterprise requests are high-touch: they frequently require quantization guidance, model-family routing changes, or dedicated capacity adjustments. Current manual triage creates delays, inconsistent prioritization, and missed SLAs for paying enterprise customers. We need a repeatable, instrumented intake that reduces manual work and routes high-impact items to the right teams quickly.
scope:
- Build a lightweight rule+ML hybrid signal classifier that runs in the intake API.
- Define lanes and explicit routing targets: self-serve (Console guides), concierge/advisory (Solutions Eng), enterprise SLA queue (Customer Success + PM), eng backlog (ENG triage).
- Telemetry signals to use: customer tier, monthly spend, request type (batching/caching/quant), observed latency/cost delta, prefix length distribution, cache hit rates, request rate anomalies, error spike correlation.
- Integrations: Slack alerts to concierge channel, create Linear tickets automatically in appropriate team queue, populate intake dashboard in Console.
acceptance_criteria:
- Automated triage correctly routes 90% of historical enterprise requests to the correct lane in a 2-week backtest across 500 historical items.
- Intake reduces average time-to-first-response for enterprise requests from 4 business days to <24 hours.
- Documentation and runbook published: intake flow, score thresholds, manual override steps.
- Dashboard shows per-lane queue length, median time-to-claim, and false-positive rate.
out_of_scope:
- Full workflow automation for Dedicated capacity provisioning (this remains a manual provisioning flow).
- Rewriting backend inference routing engine. The classifier only recommends routes and attaches metadata for engineers.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Over-reliance on heuristics may misroute edge enterprise cases. Mitigation: include manual override and conservative thresholds for high-dollar customers.
- Risk: Telemetry data lag causing stale decisions. Mitigation: use near-real-time metrics (1-5 minute windows) and degrade to manual triage when data is stale.
- Risk: Privacy/regulatory concerns for sensitive customers. Mitigation: allow customers to opt-out of automated telemetry-based routing; ensure classifier does not surface PII.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): Define signals and simple rule set; backtest on 6 months of historical requests; build Linear ticket generator and Slack integration.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Add lightweight ML model for score calibration, instrument Console dashboard, pilot with top-10 enterprise accounts.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Iterate thresholds, add exportable CSVs for PM/SE reviews, finalize runbook and train concierge teams.
monitoring_and_metrics:
- Routing accuracy (backtest baseline), current routing accuracy (live)
- Time-to-first-response by lane
- % of requests auto-resolved by self-serve suggestions
- Enterprise SLA breach rate (should decrease)
- Manual overrides by reason code
- False-positive rate (requests that needed to be re-routed)
